agentic.origin: The adjective ‘agentic’ predates generative AI. In current AI usage, it describes systems that pursue goals with limited direct supervision; OpenAI used ‘agentic AI systems’ in a 2023 governance paper, while later industry guidance helped standardize the modern sense around goal pursuit, planning, and action.

history.event: OpenAI published ‘Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems,’ defining agentic AI systems as systems that can pursue complex goals with limited direct supervision.

sources.title: Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems

ai-agent.origin: The concept of software agents is much older than modern generative AI. In current LLM usage, an AI agent generally refers to a model-centered system that directs its own process and tool use toward a user-defined goal, often operating in a loop of planning, acting, observing, and adjusting.

history.event: OpenAI’s agentic-AI governance paper described systems that can pursue complex goals with limited direct supervision.

Anthropic described an agent as an AI model that directs its own processes and tool use, repeatedly planning, acting, observing results, and adjusting until a task is complete or human input is needed.

sources.title: Practices for Governing Agentic AI Systems

context-window.origin: ‘Context window’ is an established language-model term rather than a generative-AI coinage. It refers to the amount of input context a model can reference while generating new output, functioning as a bounded working memory distinct from the model’s training corpus.

history.event: OpenAI’s API update highlighted longer-context models alongside function calling, reflecting the term’s growing practical importance as LLM applications expanded.

sources.title: Function calling and other API updates

few-shot.origin: Few-shot learning predates modern generative AI, but the term became central to large-language-model prompting through work such as the 2020 GPT-3 paper, which evaluated task performance from a small number of demonstrations supplied in text.

history.event: The GPT-3 paper ‘Language Models are Few-Shot Learners’ documented few-shot performance using examples provided in the model's text context without gradient updates.

grounding.origin: Grounding is an older AI and language-processing concept. In modern generative AI, it commonly means supplying or connecting a model to trusted external information so its response can be rooted in evidence rather than generated only from model parameters.

history.event: Google Cloud described grounding as connecting large language models with sources of truth and distinguished RAG as one specific grounding technique.

sources.title: How Vertex AI grounding helps build more reliable models

inference.origin: Inference is a long-established machine-learning term that predates generative AI. It refers to using a trained model on new input to produce predictions or outputs; in LLMs, that output is typically a generated response.

mcp.origin: Anthropic introduced and open-sourced the Model Context Protocol as an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external data sources and tools.

history.event: Anthropic publicly introduced MCP, its specification and SDKs, local server support in Claude Desktop, and an open-source repository of MCP servers.

model-collapse.origin: Researchers led by Ilia Shumailov and Zakhar Shumaylov used ‘model collapse’ for the degenerative process that can occur when generations of generative models are recursively trained on model-generated data.

history.event: Nature published ‘AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data,’ defining model collapse and reporting experiments across language models and other generative models.

sources.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data

multimodal.origin: ‘Multimodal’ predates modern generative AI and broadly describes systems that work across multiple forms of information. In current AI usage, multimodal models can understand or generate combinations of text, images, audio, video, code, or other modalities.

history.event: OpenAI documented GPT-4V as adding image input to GPT-4 and described multimodal LLMs as extending language-only systems with additional modalities.
Google introduced Gemini as a model family built from the ground up to be multimodal across text, code, audio, images, and video.

sources.title: Introducing Gemini: Google’s most capable AI model yet

prompt-injection.origin: Simon Willison coined the term ‘prompt injection’ in September 2022 after Riley Goodside demonstrated attacks that caused GPT-3 to follow malicious instructions embedded in user input.

firstKnownUse.note: Willison's post naming the attack pattern.

history.event: Riley Goodside demonstrated malicious inputs that overrode earlier GPT-3 instructions; Simon Willison published ‘Prompt injection attacks against GPT-3’ and named the pattern prompt injection.
Willison described why adding more AI-based filtering did not provide a dependable security guarantee against prompt injection.

sources.title: You can’t solve AI security problems with more AI

rag.origin: The term Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) was introduced in a 2020 research paper by Patrick Lewis and coauthors for models that combine parametric language-model memory with retrieved non-parametric memory.

firstKnownUse.note: Date of the arXiv submission for the paper that introduced the RAG formulation and name.

history.event: Lewis and coauthors submitted ‘Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks,’ introducing the RAG name and model formulation.
The work was published at NeurIPS 2020.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

reasoning-model.origin: Reasoning as an AI capability long predates current generative systems, and ‘reasoning model’ does not have a single clear origin. The modern product category gained prominence in 2024 when OpenAI introduced o1-preview as a model series trained to spend more time reasoning before responding.

history.event: OpenAI introduced o1-preview, describing a new series of models designed to spend more time thinking before responding and to perform better on complex reasoning tasks in science, coding, and mathematics.

token.origin: Tokens are an established concept in computing and natural-language processing, not a generative-AI coinage. In language models, tokenization divides text into the units the model processes, and those units may be whole words, word pieces, characters, punctuation, or other text fragments depending on the tokenizer.

tool-calling.origin: The broader idea of software invoking external functions predates LLMs. In modern generative AI, tool calling grew out of capabilities often first exposed as ‘function calling,’ where models produce structured requests that applications use to invoke external APIs or tools.

history.event: OpenAI announced function calling for GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 Turbo, allowing models to choose functions and emit structured arguments so applications could connect model outputs to external tools and APIs.

sources.title: Function calling and other API updates

vibe-coding.origin: Andrej Karpathy introduced the phrase ‘vibe coding’ in a February 2, 2025 social-media post describing a highly AI-directed style of building software in which the developer focuses on outcomes and may pay little attention to the generated code.

firstKnownUse.note: Karpathy's post is widely credited with introducing the term.

history.event: Andrej Karpathy posted ‘There’s a new kind of coding I call vibe coding,’ describing a workflow centered on conversational prompting, accepting generated changes, and focusing on whether the result works.
Merriam-Webster added a dictionary entry for ‘vibe coding,’ documenting the term's 2025 first known use and Karpathy attribution.
